public_rationale: A June 26, 2026 report described Lindy's switch from Anthropic to DeepSeek and spending restraint among other AI customers [e1]. Anthropic's October 26, 2026 filing reported customer expansion and approximately 900% net revenue retention as of September 30, 2026 [e2]. These items do not establish the required scale of customer retrenchment or achievement or failure of the three companies' applicable original long-term projections [e1, e2]. The evidence therefore leaves the conditional forecast unresolved.
limitations: The three companies, applicable original projections and threshold for 'enough' customers remain unidentified.
The customer pullback report is secondary and does not measure retrenchment across all three companies.
Anthropic's reported expansion does not establish achievement of an applicable original long-term projection.
No completed target periods or irreversible failures are documented; 'ever hit' leaves the horizon open.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If enough customers have second thoughts about AI, none of the three IPO'ing companies will ever hit their long-term projections.
conditions: if enough customers have second thoughts

statement.excerpt: If enough customers have second thoughts, none of the three IPO’ing companies will ever hit their long-term projections.
statement.document_title: If enough other companies report the same, the bubble pops. 🫧

from_speaker: If enough customers have second thoughts
none of the three IPO’ing companies
will ever hit their long-term projections
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that substantial customer retrenchment would prevent all three companies from achieving their existing long-term business projections.
Second thoughts must translate into observable cancellations, reduced purchases or nonrenewals. Expressions of concern alone do not establish the condition.
The word 'enough' supplies no threshold. It cannot fairly be defined after the fact as whatever customer loss makes the prediction true.
The supplied post does not name the three companies. Searches treated OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX as candidates, without treating their identity as established.
The relevant projections must have existed when the post was published. Later forecasts cannot silently replace them.
The financial scope below records unspecified projected business performance; it does not select revenue, profit or another particular measure.
criteria.support_condition: Establish the customer-retrenchment condition independently, identify the three companies and their original projections, and show that every company failed those projections on their stated terms. If 'ever' means eventual attainment without a target date, support requires irreversible inability to attain them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the customer-retrenchment condition is established, at least one of the three companies achieves its applicable original long-term projections on the same measurement basis.

evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes customer expansion in its discussion of September results. This cautions against treating individual customer departures as proof of broad retrenchment, but cannot settle a conditional prediction about all three companies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Identify the companies and projections that existed when the claim was published, including their metrics, measurement bases and target periods. Establish the customer-retrenchment threshold independently of subsequent results and show that it occurred. Matching results showing that one company achieved its applicable projections would contradict the forecast. Failure by all three over the original target periods would support it; if the targets concern eventual attainment without a deadline, support requires irreversible inability to attain them.
